newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling weaker vs dollar, pound.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling weaker vs dollar, pound.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling opened the market weaker against the dollar and the pound on Tuesday in quiet trading, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 53.51 against the dollar from 54.47 on Monday, while against the pound it was posted at a commercial mean of 87.82 from 87.61.
Dealers said the shilling's weakening against the dollar was due to residual demand carried forward from last week aided by exporters holding out of the market.
But they added that the shilling appeared to have steadied against the dollar at the 53.35/65 level.
"The market is pretty thin. In fact it's unusually quiet for a Tuesday," one dealer said.
Some dealers said there was not much demand for the dollar:
"In fact, what we've seen is a lot of movement against the pound probably because the dollar lost against the pound in the international market," one dealer said.
The money market eased marginally with overnight rates quoted at between 16-18 percent from Monday's 20 percent.
Dealers said they expected the market to tighten with tax payments beginning on Tuesday.
